subject: The 2AM mistake that changed everything
preview_text: One user discovered a buried feature by accident. It changed how they listen.
body_paragraphs: A user emailed me at 2AM. He was frustrated — the free version had too many ads, too much noise. He almost deleted the app. Then he tapped the wrong button. It was a small mistake, but it changed everything for him.

That button was the Auto-Apply setting. He connected his headphones, and the app boosted his volume automatically. No swiping, no tapping, no ads interrupting his podcast. He wrote back: 'I forgot the app was even there. That’s the point.'

Volume Booster Pro has a feature buried in the settings: auto-apply on headphone connect. It remembers your last slider position. Plug in, get boosted. That’s it. No notifications, no nags. Just the volume you need, exactly when you need it.

Open the app, go to Settings, and toggle Auto-Apply on. Then plug in your headphones. You’ll forget the app exists — and that’s exactly how it should be. P.S. The same user now uses the EQ to cut bass on cheap earbuds. Try it next.
